SMTO-EML-0002 — SMTO couldn't reach a Gateway that can send email

GUID: 11f7fabc-4aa5-526e-b3d7-4eb82a76cdb7
Slug: email-gateway-unavailable
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • SMTO sends email through a Gateway, the helper program it uses to run work on a computer. The Gateway was unreachable or too old to handle email, so the email step stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on the Gateway you use. Make sure the computer running it is switched on and online. Email only goes out through a connected Gateway, never directly from SMTO's server.
  2. If that Gateway shows Update available, wait for its running tasks to finish, select the Update to button that shows the new version, and confirm with Update and restart. Older Gateways can't send email; updating adds that ability, but restarting stops tasks that are still running.
  3. Before asking SMTO to send again, check the sender mailbox's Sent folder (if your provider keeps one), or ask a recipient, whether the email arrived. If the Gateway lost contact partway, the email may have gone out, and checking avoids a duplicate.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows as connected, and SMTO reports that the mail server accepted your email.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your Gateways, saying which Gateway you used. Don't type your email password into the chat to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The email service had no callable Gateway email operation, the Gateway's /email/operation route answered with an unsupported-route status (400, 404, 405, 422 or 501), or a Gateway configuration or execution error reached the email wrapper.

What this means

  • The email service lacks a callable Gateway email operation, the endpoint returns an unsupported-route response, or a Gateway/configuration exception reaches the email wrapper. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • The email service lacks a callable Gateway email operation, the endpoint returns an unsupported-route response, or a Gateway/configuration exception reaches the email wrapper.

How to diagnose it

  • Check advertised email support, endpoint status and dispatch evidence; this wrapper alone does not prove an offline Gateway.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the selected Gateway is connected and advertises the email_smtp capability; an unsupported-route status from /email/operation means the Gateway predates email support and must be updated from Settings › Setup › Gateways. For GatewayConfigurationError or GatewayExecutionError, read the Server log for the dispatch failure and check the send result's status and executed fields before any resend.
  • Select a reachable paired Gateway advertising email_smtp. Update an older Gateway before sending.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • A paired supported Gateway provides the operation and the original send outcome is reconciled before any resend.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
